name: Production Plant Data for Condition Monitoring
summary: Eight run-to-failure sequences with 25 process signals and 228,424 observations for production-plant condition monitoring. Sequences C7 and C13 each combine two ordered source files.

feature_dimensions.counting: Counts L_1–L_10, A_1–A_5, B_1–B_5, and C_1–C_5. Timestamp and loader-added sample, sequence_id, and source_file columns are excluded.

sequence_statistics.description: Computed from the eight complete sequences returned by inventory(). Sample counts include missing rows. Lengths are observation counts, not physical durations.

attributes.name: Timestamp
attributes.description: Original per-file observation index, preserved verbatim including resets at joined part boundaries. Use sample for a continuous sequence index.

attributes.name: L_1..L_10
attributes.description: Source process-signal family. Values and names are preserved; physical units and detailed channel semantics are not established by the CSV files.

attributes.name: A_1..A_5
attributes.description: Source process-signal family. Values and names are preserved; physical units and detailed channel semantics are not established by the CSV files.

attributes.name: B_1..B_5
attributes.description: Source process-signal family. Values and names are preserved; physical units and detailed channel semantics are not established by the CSV files.

attributes.name: C_1..C_5
attributes.description: Source process-signal family. Values and names are preserved; physical units and detailed channel semantics are not established by the CSV files.

attributes.name: sample
attributes.description: Zero-based continuous row index across all parts of the loaded sequence.

attributes.name: sequence_id
attributes.description: Sequence number after C: 7, 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 15, or 16. Use this ID for Leave-One-Out splits.

attributes.name: source_file
attributes.description: Original CSV filename for each row; preserves source-part boundaries.

notes: The evaluation unit is a complete sequence: eight sequences and eight Leave-One-Out folds. Ten CSVs are the underlying storage files, not ten independent sequences.
The number after C is the sequence ID. Hyphenated parts are concatenated in order: C7-1 then C7-2, and C13-1 then C13-2.
Leave-One-Out evaluation holds out one complete sequence in each of eight folds. Source parts of a sequence must remain in the same fold.
The loader preserves all measurement values and missing rows, adds a continuous sample index, and retains the original Timestamp and source_file. It does not infer interruption duration.
Sequences C7, C14, and C15 each contain four rows missing all 25 signals (12 rows and 300 missing values in total). These rows are retained in sequence lengths.
The provider describes run-to-failure experiments. For an endpoint-based RUL benchmark, derive remaining sample count from the complete sequence endpoint rather than individual file endpoints.
Explicit per-sample wear, fault, and state annotations are not distributed. Timestamp physical units are not established by the CSVs.
The provider describes selecting eight features for an analysis; the raw recording schema contains 25 process signals.
citation: von Birgelen, A. et al. (2018). Self-Organizing Maps for Anomaly Localization and Predictive Maintenance in Cyber-Physical Production Systems.
